attributes.assistantPrompt: Cancel the 11:00 talk and add a coffee break at 10:30.
attributes.successCriteria:
1. `sessions` of `Conference/devday` holds, in time order, the 09:00 and 10:00 talks, a 10:30 coffee break, and the 13:00 and 14:00 talks, each talk's `title` unchanged; the 11:00 talk is gone.
2. In the indexed document every remaining talk links to its own seed speaker: 09:00 Ana Silva, 10:00 Ben Okoro, 13:00 Dev Patel, 14:00 Erin Walsh. The coffee break links to no speaker.
3. Chloé Martin (the cancelled talk's speaker) is linked from nowhere on the card, and every Speaker card is byte-identical to the seed.
4. The definition module (`card-mutation/list-links/conference.gts`) is byte-identical to the seed, and the change was made in place: the same instance file, with the same `adoptsFrom`, and no new instance written beside it.
5. The changed card is shown on screen afterwards and renders with no error boundary; every tool call applied or was repaired by the model, and the assistant did not ask a question or wait for confirmation before acting.

cardInfo.name: Card mutation: insert into and remove from a list whose items link to cards
cardInfo.summary: A Conference card is open with five sessions in a containsMany, each linking to its own Speaker card. The prompt cancels one talk and adds a coffee break before it. This eval tests whether every remaining talk keeps its own speaker after the list changes shape.
cardInfo.notes:
Use case: card mutation. The task changes card data only; every field it needs already exists, so an edit to the definition module is wrong. Judge each criterion by comparing the card's seed (in `session.json`'s bundle) with its file under `files` and its indexed document under `cards` in the workspace snapshot. The runner counts a card in `expectedChangedCards` as rendered only once its file differs from the seed.

The trap criterion is 2. A link inside a list item is stored under the item's position (`sessions.2.speaker`), and `realm.cards.update` rewrites the list without touching `relationships`, so after an insert or a removal every later talk silently points at the wrong speaker while the card renders fine. A correct run also rewrites the `sessions.N.speaker` keys with `realm.fs.replace`. Known gap: links inside containsMany items do not move with their items when the list is updated. The skills don't tell the model this, so the criterion is expected to fail until a skill or tool handles it; read a low score there as the gap, not the model.
